Load it with ToolSearch (select:Artifact) before writing any document, plan, analysis or visual, and whenever other people come up as readers, even after the work is written. Its description says whether to publish, offer a page or do neither. What follows applies whether or not it is loaded yet. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it.

attachment.content:
- animation-vocabulary: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.
- apple-design: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.
- emil-design-eng: This skill encodes Emil Kowalski's philosophy on UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- self-code-review: Deep, evidence-based self review of the current branch against its base. Use when the user asks to "self review", "review my branch", "review my PR", "review my code", "review my changes", or wants a thorough pre-push critique.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own.   functionality without a clear reason.

  implementation or adding packages. Do not assume a library lacks a
  capability without checking its documentation and types.

  that only works for now and is meant to be replaced later.
- No em-dashes in prose or user-facing copy.

  fewer. Explain only when asked.
- Surface non-trivial design decisions before baking them into a plan or an
  implementation.

Steffen Grabert, steffen.grabert@tum.de

TUM student. Python for data, ML and finance; TypeScript for web and
desktop. Recurring domains: investing and portfolio modelling, football
analytics, study tools.

# AGENTS.md

Rules for AI coding agents working in this repo. Humans follow them too.

- Hackathon repo (EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026). Code freeze and Live Final
  Sunday 12:00. Working agent first, polish second.
- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding
  compatibility layers, fallbacks, or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement.
  No speculative abstractions, configuration, or indirection.
- Grow the system in layers: smallest version that works end to end, then add on
  top of a product that already works. Never trade a working product for
  unfinished complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
- Prefer established libraries already in the project before adding new ones or
  writing your own implementation. Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper:
  the cost function, quote parsing, data lookup and the runners already exist.
- Never commit secrets. Keys go into `.env` (gitignored). Never print, log or paste the
  arena key anywhere (code, logs, issues, Discord, PR text).
- All changes go through a pull request against `main`, reviewed by one teammate.
  Branch naming: `<firstname>/<topic>`. Agents may commit, push their branch and open the PR
  (`gh pr create`) on their own; they never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
- No em-dashes in prose or user-facing copy.
- Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines or fewer.

## Challenge: Tacto Negotiation Arena

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a fictional German pump maker. Our agent
negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes
one term sheet per case, or walks away. Full text: `docs/challenge.md` (brief), `docs/api.md`
(API, claim checks, cost formula), `docs/submission.md`. Upstream:
https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit, FAQ: https://arena.tacto.ai/faq.

**Score.** Per case `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is the total
cost in euros over the case horizon: price, uncovered need, payment terms, freight, lead time,
quality, tooling, index clause, and in `stabilise` / `secure_supply` cases a charge for leaving
the supplier below a sustainable margin. Not price. `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C exactly.
No deal scores the alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.

**Live Final.** Sunday 12:00, five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, all cases of a wave in
parallel. New suppliers; up to a third combine supplier and case types practice never shows.
Some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release. Wave score = mean case score x 100; total = sum.

**Hard rules (breaking one can disqualify us):**
- No human in the loop during the final. The runner is started before 12:00 and left alone.
- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`. Those are for people.
- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams.
- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.

**Hard limits:**
- 60 seconds per message per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A late message is a
  timeout; three in a row end the thread. Heavy work happens before a session is opened.
- 10 messages per thread (case `round_limit`), up to 3 term sheets per message, every term sheet
  carries every `negotiable` field.
- Max 3 claim checks per message; one argument per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence.
  An unknown ID or wrong figure is `contradicted` and costs trust.
- 10 calls per second and 10 open sessions per key.
- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team, shared across all
  machines.** Sandbox (`case:D01`, `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.

## Repo map

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `buyer/agent.py` | which agent plays a case; our strategy grows here (today: the kit's `LLMAgent`) |
| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
| `docs/` | brief, API, submission guide (copied from upstream) |
| `data/package/` | the data package, gitignored; `uv run arena data` fetches it (Sunday also `data/release-sunday/`) |
| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office, gitignored; `uv run buyer pull` fetches them |

`arena_kit` (Tacto's starter kit) is a git dependency pinned in `pyproject.toml`. We do not patch
it; we wrap it. Its README is the best guide to its modules:
https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
uv run arena data                               # data package into data/ (again Sunday after 08:00)
uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .         # before every PR
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free, real supplier bots
uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all 10 hosted practice cases: costs 10
uv run buyer pull --set practice                # every finished session -> logs/sessions/
uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10      # the Live Final, Sunday before 12:00
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API with a scripted supplier
```

`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours. The MCP server `arena-data`
(`.mcp.json`) gives coding agents SQL, ID lookup and documents over the data package.

## Working on the negotiation agent

- **Code owns numbers, the model owns words.** Every binding value (term sheets, accept,
  walk away) is computed or checked in code with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`. Every figure
  in an e-mail comes from code, next to its data ID. The model reads the supplier and writes.
- **Never accept** a term sheet that breaks a must-have or costs more than the alternative.
  Price unstated fields at the supplier's standard terms from its quote PDF (`docs.standard_terms`).
- **Generalise, don't memorise.** No logic keyed on practice case IDs or supplier IDs. Knowledge
  derived from the data package at runtime is fine; it must also work for unseen suppliers.
- **Read the supplier.** What moves it is in the data: call notes, letters, news, quote
  remarks, payment history, scorecards. Trade what is cheap for us (payment days, contract
  length, volume, dates) for what it values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, budget, a missing alternative or the target price.
- **Every model call has a hard timeout** well under 60 s, and the move still goes out if it
  fails. Measure latency per move.

## The learning loop

1. Try on the simulator or the sandbox first. Spend practice quota only on a change you expect
   to help, and check `uv run arena me` before batch runs: teammates share the 200.
2. After practice: `uv run buyer pull`, then read `logs/sessions/`. The trace holds the supplier's
   reasons for every move, the back office its internal discussion, the result the cost breakdown.
3. Find why C_deal missed C_best (which lever, which argument, which timing), change the agent,
   score candidate term sheets offline with `total_cost`, then play again.
4. Write what you learned about supplier behaviour into the PR description, so the team and
   the pitch can use it.

## Sunday

- 08:00: `uv run arena data` again; the release lands in `data/release-sunday/`.
- 09:00: pre-flight, one practice case through the final machine and setup.
- 11:30: checklist in `docs/submission.md` (key, data, LLM credits, power, no sleep, log file).
- Before 12:00: start `uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v 2>&1 | tee logs/final.log`
  from `main`, submit that commit hash on ehl.gg.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

# Hollerau Pumpenwerke - procurement data package v1.0.0

You are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, a fictional pump maker (start with
`company.md`). Everything is as of **2026-09-30**. Company data is synthetic; market series are real
open data (`ATTRIBUTION.md`). All company names are fictional; any match with a real company is
coincidental.

## Files
- `data/*.csv` - the master copy (UTF-8, comma, ISO dates, dot decimals); schema in `datapackage.json`.
- `world.sqlite` - the same tables in one SQLite file, generated from the CSVs.
- `facts.json` - every ID you can cite in a claim, with the values the arena checks.
- Prices are per `price_unit` (1, 100 or 1,000 pieces, kg or m), as the ERP states them; cases
  negotiate in the same unit.
- `company.md`, `SCORECARD.md`, `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, `ATTRIBUTION.md`; contract texts in `contracts/`,
  letters, e-mails and notes in `correspondence/`.

## IDs
`<type>:<id>[@period]`, unique across the package, in the first column of each table: `sup:70110`,
`part:310010`, `po:4500010001-10`, `gr:`, `inv:`, `qn:`, `ctr:4600070110` (clause `ctr:4600070110#3.1`),
`quote:`, `rfq:`, `fc:310010@2026-09`, `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `cost:310010`,
`news:`, `doc:`.

## Tables
| Table | Rows | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `suppliers` | 447 | Vendor master: the detailed suppliers (`detail = full`) and the long tail (`spend only`). |
| `supplier_intel` | 46 | Public face of each detailed supplier: register facts, filed turnover, credit index, audit. |
| `parts` | 60 | Material master of the detailed parts. |
| `sourcing` | 90 | Source list: approved suppliers per part, quota, tooling owner. |
| `price_conditions` | 339 | Price history per part and supplier (price per `price_unit`), with the event behind it. |
| `negotiation_history` | 300 | Past price events: renewals with asked and settled change. |
| `contracts` | 46 | Framework agreements (text in `contracts/`). |
| `contract_clauses` | 280 | Clauses of the framework agreements, incl. index clauses (`ctr:<no>#<clause>`). |
| `po_lines` | 5400 | Purchase order lines: requested and first confirmed date, price per `price_unit`. |
| `goods_receipts` | 5580 | Goods receipts per PO line (posting date, quantity). |
| `invoices` | 5578 | Supplier invoices with due and payment dates, cash discount taken. |
| `quality_notifications` | 1033 | Complaints against suppliers (QN), with 8D dates and recharged fees. |
| `scorecards` | 414 | Rolling 12-month supplier scorecards per quarter (method: `SCORECARD.md`). |
| `forecasts` | 720 | Quarterly demand forecast snapshots per part, shared with suppliers. |
| `forecast_lines` | 8640 | Monthly quantities of each forecast snapshot. |
| `rfqs` | 47 | Requests for quotation: past benchmarks, second-source quotes, open RFQs for new parts. |
| `quotes` | 108 | Supplier quotes (price per `price_unit`); missing fields as the supplier sent them. |
| `spend_cube` | 1137 | Spend per fiscal year and supplier, incl. the long tail. |
| `index_series` | 33 | Market series: source, licence, unit; derived series with their formula. |
| `index_values` | 2258 | Monthly values of the market series (`idx:<series>@<YYYY-MM>`). |
| `cost_drivers` | 166 | The category team's estimate of each part's cost drivers (index series and weight). |
| `should_cost` | 28 | Bottom-up should-cost estimates for selected parts (`cost:<part>`). |
| `news` | 39 | Press items about suppliers and markets. |
| `documents` | 208 | Letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes (text in `correspondence/`). |

## How the tables connect
```
suppliers 1-n sourcing n-1 parts          parts 1-n price_conditions n-1 suppliers
suppliers 1-1 supplier_intel, 1-n contracts 1-n contract_clauses
po_lines -> goods_receipts -> invoices;   goods_receipts 1-n quality_notifications
parts 1-n forecasts 1-n forecast_lines;   rfqs 1-n quotes;   index_series 1-n index_values
suppliers -> scorecards, spend_cube, news, documents;   parts -> cost_drivers, should_cost
```

## Example queries (SQLite)
```sql
-- spend by supplier, last fiscal year
SELECT s.name, c.spend_eur FROM spend_cube c JOIN suppliers s ON s.id = c.supplier_id
WHERE c.fiscal_year = 'FY2026' ORDER BY c.spend_eur DESC LIMIT 10;
-- price history of one part
SELECT supplier_id, valid_from, price, price_unit FROM price_conditions WHERE part_id = 'part:310010';
-- latest scorecard per supplier
SELECT supplier_id, otd_pct, ppm, colour FROM scorecards WHERE quarter = '2026Q3' ORDER BY score;
-- an index over the last year
SELECT month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = 'PPI-C2451' AND month >= '2025-08';
-- how late Hollerau pays a supplier
SELECT AVG(julianday(paid_date) - julianday(due_date)) FROM invoices
WHERE supplier_id = 'sup:70210' AND discount_taken = 0 AND paid_date IS NOT NULL;
```
# Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH

Family-owned pump maker from Hollerau, Lower Bavaria, Germany, founded 1952, owned by the Stangl family (third generation). Revenue about
EUR 252 M, 910 employees, one plant. Fiscal year October to September.

## Products
- **HN**: HN standard water pumps (EN 733)
- **HB**: HB building-services inline pumps
- **HI**: HI industrial process pumps, stainless (ISO 5199)
- **HX**: HX high-efficiency series (start of production 2027-03)

## Purchasing
You are the purchasing team for the pump line's parts and materials (about EUR 35 M in FY2026, see
`spend_cube.csv`). The detailed data covers the 46 suppliers and 60 parts that matter most.

## Policies
- Standard payment terms: 60 days net. Cost of capital for valuing payment terms:
  8% a year.
- Approval: deals above EUR 250 k a year need the head of purchasing, above EUR 1 M the managing director.
- A-parts are dual-sourced where a qualified second source exists (`sourcing.csv`).
- Quality agreement with every series supplier: on-time delivery target 95 %, flat fee of
  EUR 150 per supplier-caused complaint, 8D report within 60 days.
- Preferred Incoterm: DAP Hollerau. Freight for EXW/FCA deliveries is booked by Hollerau.

## Should-cost
`should_cost.csv` estimates full cost without margin. For the parts of strategic and bottleneck
negotiations the category team modelled the current supplier's own plant (`supplier_id`, error about
5 %); the other rows use a German cost base with an error of 5-15 %. Rule of thumb for other countries'
full cost relative to Germany: AT and CH about 1.0-1.1, CZ, PL and HU about 0.8-0.85, TR about 0.75,
CN about 0.7.

## Category strategies
Every negotiation states its category goal (`stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage`, `routine`); the rates of its cost C follow it.
Quality escalations are `quality_first`, capacity squeezes `secure_supply`, kits and bundles `routine`.

| Category | Strategy | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| castings | secure supply and energy-cost transparency; build Central-European second sources | stabilise |
| machined parts | leverage: competition between local job shops, bundle small parts | leverage |
| sheet metal | leverage; quality first after the 2026 base-frame issues | leverage |
| seals | bottleneck: long-term agreements, qualify second sources where approvals allow | secure_supply |
| electrical | strategic: copper and electronics clauses, multi-year frameworks | stabilise |
| C-parts | routine: fewer suppliers, kits, lower process cost | routine |
| raw material | index-based pricing, negotiate base price and extras | leverage |

## Targets for FY2027
Material cost -3 % against the index-adjusted baseline; no supplier in red for more than two quarters.
# Known issues

The data is shaped like a real ERP extract, quirks included. None of these are errors to report.

1. Three delivery dates per PO line: requested, first confirmed and the goods-receipt posting date. OTD
   differs by 10-30 points depending on the reference date.
2. Goods receipts are posted on working days only (weekends, Bavarian holidays, August shutdown).
3. Partial deliveries (two receipts per line) and small over-deliveries within 5 %.
4. C-parts, some raw material and the motor cable are priced per 100 or per 1,000 units (`price_unit`);
   a PO line's value is qty x price / price_unit.
5. One supplier sits twice in the vendor master: `sup:71999` is the old record of `sup:70210` (renamed 2024).
6. A few PO lines use an outdated price (`price_note = stale_condition`): purchase price variance.
7. Index clauses are in `contract_clauses.csv` and in the contract text (`contracts/`).
8. Past quotes miss fields where the supplier left them out (`missing_fields`).
9. Invoices are paid late for some suppliers; a few cash discounts were taken after the discount period.
10. Complaints on small lots make PPM jumpy; read the rolling scorecard, not single lots.
11. PO lines with requested dates after 2026-09-30 are open orders without receipts.
12. Index series end at different months: each source publishes with its own lag (`index_series.csv`).
13. Small suppliers file no profit and loss account: `supplier_intel.csv` gives their turnover as a band.
14. Should-cost (`should_cost.csv`) assumes a German cost base and has an error of 5-15 %.
15. The spend cube holds about 400 further suppliers known only by name, category and spend.
# Supplier scorecard - method

Each row (`sc:<supplier>@<quarter>`) covers the rolling 12 months to the end of that quarter and is sent to
the supplier, so both sides know it.

- **otd_pct**: share of goods-receipt lines posted between 5 days before and 2 days after the
  requested date of the PO line. **otd_confirmed_pct**: the same against the supplier's first confirmed date.
  Partial deliveries count as separate lines.
- **ppm**: supplier-caused complaint quantity / received quantity x 1,000,000 (complaints by date of the QN).
- **open_8d_overdue**: supplier-caused complaints older than 60 days without a closed 8D report at quarter end.
- **score** = 0.5 x otd_pct + 0.5 x quality points - 5 x open_8d_overdue, with quality points =
  100 x max(0, 1 - ppm / 10,000).
- **class / colour**: A green >= 85, B amber 70-84.9, C red < 70.
   9 .

 208 ./correspondence
  24 ./data

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

=== 20260911-70110-P01
# Price adjustment from 01 November 2026

letter - 2026-09-11 - Gießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG

Dear Sir or Madam,

we have supplied Hollerau Pumpenwerke reliably for many years. Owing to sustained increases in energy, raw material and wage costs, we are forced to adjust our prices for Volute casing HN 50-200 (part:310010) by **9.5 %** with effect from **01 November 2026**: from EUR 126.53 to EUR 138.55 per  pc.

We regret this step and ask for your understanding.

Yours faithfully,
Gießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG

=== 20260804-70150-M4
# Liquidity

call note - 2026-08-04 - Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing

Call with the managing director of Tarsevi Döküm Sanayi A.Ş.: he asked twice whether we could pay earlier and said the bank is watching every month. 'I cannot sign anything that lowers our margin now.'

=== 20260909-70110-M4
# Visit by the owner

meeting note - 2026-09-09 - Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing

The owner of Gießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG admitted he had not followed his material and energy prices closely since the 2022 peak; his office manager does the costing.

=== 20260913-70430-P15
# One supplier for the kit

memo - 2026-09-13 - Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing

Kit per unit (about 25000 kits a year):
- 2 x O-ring set EPDM, drinking-water approved (part:340020)
- 1 x Casing gasket, aramid fibre (part:340030)
- 2 x Lip seal 35x52x7 (part:340040)

Today these parts come from several suppliers. We want one supplier for the kit.

=== 20260921-70140-P11
# Escalation: delivery and quality performance

letter - 2026-09-21 - Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Supplier Quality

To Odlewnia Kalwisz Sp. z o.o.

your rolling 12-month scorecard (sc:70140@2026Q3) is **red**: on-time delivery 63.5 %, 2376 ppm, 0 overdue 8D reports. We expect a binding improvement plan for Bearing bracket HN (part:310020) and will discuss quality commitments and cost recovery.

Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Supplier Quality

=== 20260915-70220-P09
# Capacity situation and delivery dates

email - 2026-09-15 - CNC-Technik Obermaier & Huber GmbH

Hello,

due to very high capacity utilisation we cannot confirm your full forecast for Flange DN 65 PN 16, machined (part:320030) for the coming months. Lead times are currently longer than agreed. We will prioritise customers with firm, long-term commitments.

Best regards,
CNC-Technik Obermaier & Huber GmbH

=== 20260912-70710-P08
# Price basis and surcharge clause for the coming period

letter - 2026-09-12 - Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

Dear Sir or Madam,

for Round bar 1.4404 dia 30 mm, peeled (part:370010) we propose to agree the price basis for the coming period, including a price adjustment clause based on AS-14404. Please let us know your view.

Yours faithfully,
Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

=== 20260913-70260-M2
# Payment of invoices

email - 2026-09-13 - Mechanik Tauvelt GmbH

Could you pay our invoices within 10 days? In return we would grant a cash discount.

"""The published cost function: what a term sheet costs the buyer in €, plus term helpers.

C covers the buyer's fixed need over a fixed horizon: need the deal does not cover is bought at
the case's fallback price (plus the fallback risk of the category goal), committed volume is bought
needed or not, and units bought before a new price takes effect cost the current price. In
strategic and bottleneck cases a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin costs
too - pass your estimate of the supplier (`supplier_value`) to price that. Do the arithmetic here,
not in the language model.
"""

import math
import operator
from datetime import date

# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.
RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}
OPS = {
    "<=": operator.le,
    "<": operator.lt,
    ">=": operator.ge,
    ">": operator.gt,
    "==": operator.eq,
    "!=": operator.ne,
}


def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    """
    b = case["buyer"]
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan = {
        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    }
    t = dict(plan)
    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    return t


def horizon_start(case):
    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None


def _years(case, t):
    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    months = t["contract_months"]
    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])


def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    years = _years(case, t)
    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
        - freight[std["incoterm"]]  # it carries the freight leg
        + ((t.get("tooling_eur") or 0) - (std.get("tooling_eur") or 0)) / sold * cash_now
        - ppm / 1e6 * ((t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) - (std.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0))
        + supplier.get("extra", 0.0)
    )


def _soft(gap):
    """Margin points below the sustainable margin, as they cost: none above it, quadratic over
    the first 5 points, linear beyond - no kink."""
    if gap <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return gap * gap / 10 if gap <= 5 else gap - 2.5


def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your
    estimate of its full cost; `value` overrides `supplier_value`. Without an estimate: 0."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    per_point, sustainable = b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"), b.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
    if b.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not per_point or not sustainable or not supplier:
        return 0.0
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    worth = value if value is not None else supplier_value(case, t, supplier)
    margin = (worth - supplier["full_cost"]) / worth * 100
    return per_point * _soft(sustainable - margin) * _years(case, t)


def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""
    b, t = case["buyer"], closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    if t.get("unit_price") is None:
        raise ValueError("no unit_price: a term sheet without a price has no cost")
    years = _years(case, t)
    committed = t["volume_per_year"] * years  # bought, needed or not
    covered = min(t["volume_per_year"], b["need_per_year"]) * years
    pre = _units_before(case, t, years)
    at_new_price = (committed - pre) * t["unit_price"]
    spend = pre * (b.get("current_unit_price") or t["unit_price"]) + at_new_price
    per_defect = b.get("cost_per_defect", 0)
    defect_cost = per_defect - min(t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0, per_defect)
    index = index_risk = 0.0
    if clause := t.get("index_clause"):
        path = b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause["series"], 0.0)
        moved = max(0.0, abs(path) - clause["deadband_pct"] / 100)
        index = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * moved * math.copysign(1, path)
        index_risk = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100
    uncovered = (b["need_per_year"] * b["horizon_years"] - covered) * b["fallback_unit_price"]
    need = b["need_lead_time_days"]
    return {
        "price": spend,
        "uncovered_need": uncovered,
        "fallback_risk": uncovered * b.get("fallback_risk_pct", 0) / 100,
        "payment_terms": spend * b["interest_rate"] * (b["reference_payment_days"] - t["payment_days"]) / 360,
        "freight": committed * b["freight_eur_per_unit"][t["incoterm"]],
        "late_delivery": b.get("late_cost_per_day", 0) * max(0, t["lead_time_days"] - need),
        "quality": committed * (t.get("ppm_commitment") or 0) / 1e6 * defect_cost,
        "tooling": t.get("tooling_eur") or 0.0,
        "index_clause": index,
        "index_risk": index_risk,
        "relationship": relationship_cost(case, t, supplier=supplier),
    }


def total_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C in EUR; infinite for terms without a price (e.g. a supplier that quotes none), so such a
    sheet is never the cheapest and never beats an alternative."""
    if closing_terms(case, terms, standard).get("unit_price") is None:
        return math.inf
    return round(sum(cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard, supplier).values()), 2)


def score(c_open, c_deal, c_best):
    if c_deal is None:
        return 0.0
    if c_open - c_best <= 0.01:  # no room to negotiate: matching the best is full marks
        return 1.0 if c_deal <= c_best + 0.01 else 0.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, (c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)))


def must_haves_ok(case, terms, standard=None):
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []):
        value = t.get(m["field"])
        if value is None and m["op"] not in ("==", "!="):
            return False
        if not OPS[m["op"]](value, m["value"]):
            return False
    return True


def snap(case, field, value):
    """The allowed value closest to `value` (case `term_options`), else `value` unchanged."""
    options = case.get("term_options", {}).get(field)
    if not options or value in options:
        return value
    if isinstance(value, int | float) and all(isinstance(o, int | float) for o in options):
        return min(options, key=lambda o: (abs(o - value), o))
    return options[0]


def complete_offer(case, terms):
    """A valid term sheet: exactly the negotiable fields, gaps from the buyer's plan, snapped."""
    plan = closing_terms(case, {"unit_price": None})
    freight = case["buyer"]["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan["incoterm"] = min(freight, key=freight.get)  # when asking, ask for the cheapest freight
    out = {}
    for field in case["negotiable"]:
        value = terms.get(field, plan.get(field))
        if value is None and case.get("term_options", {}).get(field):
            value = case["term_options"][field][0]
        value = snap(case, field, value)
        out[field] = round(value, 2) if field == "unit_price" and value is not None else value
    return out

"""The published cost function: what a term sheet costs the buyer in €, plus term helpers.

C covers the buyer's fixed need over a fixed horizon: need the deal does not cover is bought at
the case's fallback price (plus the fallback risk of the category goal), committed volume is bought
needed or not, and units bought before a new price takes effect cost the current price. In
strategic and bottleneck cases a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin costs
too - pass your estimate of the supplier (`supplier_value`) to price that. Do the arithmetic here,
not in the language model.
"""

import math
import operator
from datetime import date

# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.
RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}
OPS = {
    "<=": operator.le,
    "<": operator.lt,
    ">=": operator.ge,
    ">": operator.gt,
    "==": operator.eq,
    "!=": operator.ne,
}


def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    """
    b = case["buyer"]
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan = {
        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    }
    t = dict(plan)
    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    return t


def horizon_start(case):
    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None


def _years(case, t):
    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    months = t["contract_months"]
    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])


def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    years = _years(case, t)
    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
        - freight[std["incoterm"]]  # it carries the freight leg
        + ((t.get("tooling_eur") or 0) - (std.get("tooling_eur") or 0)) / sold * cash_now
        - ppm / 1e6 * ((t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) - (std.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0))
        + supplier.get("extra", 0.0)
    )


def _soft(gap):
    """Margin points below the sustainable margin, as they cost: none above it, quadratic over
    the first 5 points, linear beyond - no kink."""
    if gap <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return gap * gap / 10 if gap <= 5 else gap - 2.5


def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your
    estimate of its full cost; `value` overrides `supplier_value`. Without an estimate: 0."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    per_point, sustainable = b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"), b.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
    if b.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not per_point or not sustainable or not supplier:
        return 0.0
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    worth = value if value is not None else supplier_value(case, t, supplier)
    margin = (worth - supplier["full_cost"]) / worth * 100
    return per_point * _soft(sustainable - margin) * _years(case, t)


def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""

    if t.get("unit_price") is None:
        raise ValueError("no unit_price: a term sheet without a price has no cost")
    years = _years(case, t)
    committed = t["volume_per_year"] * years  # bought, needed or not
    covered = min(t["volume_per_year"], b["need_per_year"]) * years
    pre = _units_before(case, t, years)
    at_new_price = (committed - pre) * t["unit_price"]
    spend = pre * (b.get("current_unit_price") or t["unit_price"]) + at_new_price
    per_defect = b.get("cost_per_defect", 0)
    defect_cost = per_defect - min(t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0, per_defect)
    index = index_risk = 0.0
    if clause := t.get("index_clause"):
        path = b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause["series"], 0.0)
        moved = max(0.0, abs(path) - clause["deadband_pct"] / 100)
        index = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * moved * math.copysign(1, path)
        index_risk = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100
    uncovered = (b["need_per_year"] * b["horizon_years"] - covered) * b["fallback_unit_price"]
    need = b["need_lead_time_days"]
    return {
        "price": spend,
        "uncovered_need": uncovered,
        "fallback_risk": uncovered * b.get("fallback_risk_pct", 0) / 100,
        "payment_terms": spend * b["interest_rate"] * (b["reference_payment_days"] - t["payment_days"]) / 360,
        "freight": committed * b["freight_eur_per_unit"][t["incoterm"]],
        "late_delivery": b.get("late_cost_per_day", 0) * max(0, t["lead_time_days"] - need),
        "quality": committed * (t.get("ppm_commitment") or 0) / 1e6 * defect_cost,
        "tooling": t.get("tooling_eur") or 0.0,
        "index_clause": index,
        "index_risk": index_risk,
        "relationship": relationship_cost(case, t, supplier=supplier),
    }


def total_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C in EUR; infinite for terms without a price (e.g. a supplier that quotes none), so such a
    sheet is never the cheapest and never beats an alternative."""
    if closing_terms(case, terms, standard).get("unit_price") is None:
        return math.inf
    return round(sum(cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard, supplier).values()), 2)


def score(c_open, c_deal, c_best):
    if c_deal is None:
        return 0.0

        return 1.0 if c_deal <= c_best + 0.01 else 0.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, (c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)))


def must_haves_ok(case, terms, standard=None):
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []):
        value = t.get(m["field"])
        if value is None and m["op"] not in ("==", "!="):
            return False
        if not OPS[m["op"]](value, m["value"]):
            return False
    return True

    """The allowed value closest to `value` (case `term_options`), else `value` unchanged."""
    options = case.get("term_options", {}).get(field)
    if not options or value in options:
        return value
    if isinstance(value, int | float) and all(isinstance(o, int | float) for o in options):
        return min(options, key=lambda o: (abs(o - value), o))
    return options[0]


def complete_offer(case, terms):
    """A valid term sheet: exactly the negotiable fields, gaps from the buyer's plan, snapped."""
    plan = closing_terms(case, {"unit_price": None})
    freight = case["buyer"]["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan["incoterm"] = min(freight, key=freight.get)  # when asking, ask for the cheapest freight
    out = {}

            value = case["term_options"][field][0]
        value = snap(case, field, value)
        out[field] = round(value, 2) if field == "unit_price" and value is not None else value
    return out

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |
